replacement_text: Global marine cargo insurance premiums reached USD 22.64 billion in 2024 (IUMI Stats Report 2025, primary data), a 1.6% increase year-on-year. Asia/Pacific accounted for 35.15% of global cargo premiums (~USD 7.96 billion), the fastest-growing major region at +8.8% YoY, driven principally by China's 17.6% market share — itself underpinned by e-commerce growth and return-insurance schemes. The global marine insurance book across all lines (cargo, hull, offshore energy, marine liability) totalled USD 39.92 billion in 2024.
notes: All six granular sub-figures in the original draft (22.64B, 35.15%, 7.96B, 8.8%, 17.6%, 39.92B) are directly confirmed from the IUMI Stats Report 2025 PDF (downloaded, markitdown-converted, and read in full). The validator concern about the prior IUMI PDF fetch failure is resolved: the 2025 report PDF (which carries 2024 data) was successfully downloaded and converted. The 8.8% figure specifically refers to Asia/Pacific cargo premium growth, not overall marine growth — that nuance is preserved in the replacement text. The original draft's attribution to 'IUMI primary data' is accurate and appropriate. No NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH tags required. Cross-validation: IUMI press release (official) and IUMI Facts & Figures 2024 page both independently confirm the headline figures.
